text:
Josh Morrissey missed more than a month with an upper-body injury, from October 7 until the Jets activated him for the November 10 game against New Jersey. Winnipeg won both games since he returned, and he played 24 minutes in each, as if he'd never left.

Six games is too small a sample to say much about this season, so his track record carries the weight. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th of 215 defensemen in value last season, most of it from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 86th percentile for setting up teammates' shots. He has four assists and no goals so far, which is about what his chances say (0.8 expected goals).

What matters now is minutes. A healthy Morrissey eats the hardest 24 a night on the Jets' blue line and runs a power-play unit, which pushes everyone else into roles they fit. His skating numbers from NHL Edge are low, but they come from a short stretch around an injury. Judge him in December.
headline: Morrissey is back, and Winnipeg needed him
